newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopian Insurance to pay crash victims, airline.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopian Insurance to pay crash victims, airline.

text.p: State-owned Ethiopian Insurance Company said on Thursday it would pay full compensation to the families of the 125 people who died after a hijacked Ethiopian Airlines plane crashed on Saturday.
It also said it would pay $40 million to cover a claim by the airline for the Boeing 767 plane wrecked in the crash off the Comoro Islands.
"The $40 million is payable for the aircraft for which it had been insured," Haile Micheal Kumsa, general manager of the company, told reporters.
The medical expenses of those injured and other costs, covering transportation of bodies and burial expenses, for example, would also be paid.
Haile Micheal said the company would pay compensation to third parties that might have suffered as a result of the crash.
He said the payout would be the highest in the company's history.
Ethiopian Insurance is reinsured with major international reinsurers, including some in the Lloyd's of London market.
There were 175 passengers and crew on the plane that crashed after being hijacked between Addis Ababa and Nairobi. Fifty people survived.
Ethiopian Airlines officials said identifying the 125 killed had proved harder than anticipated.

Bodies recovered from the aircraft and sea carried little to help identification, and investigators were continuing the painstaking process with the help of recent photos of passengers, where available.
